disease_label_per_paper: Giant cell arteritis with atypical fever and bilateral headache presentation
presentation_summary: 73-year-old man presented with 10 days of bilateral headache radiating to the occipital area with fevers, persistent chills, generalized weakness, and minor neck-flexion pain.
He denied visual changes, diplopia, loss of vision, floaters, jaw claudication, trismus, hip or shoulder stiffness, arthralgia, dyspnea, and cough.
Initial labs/vitals showed WBC 17 K/uL, ESR 108 mm/hr, CRP 28.9 mg/L, oral temperature 100.0 F, BP 125/80 mmHg, HR 108/min, and RR 16/min.

During admission he developed swelling, sharp pain, sensitivity to palpation, and erythema in the temporal, periorbital, and glabellar regions with rhinorrhea and sinus tenderness; CT sinus showed minimal mucosal disease.
Bilateral temporal artery biopsy later showed active non-granulomatous vasculitis compatible with bilateral temporal arteritis in the clinical setting.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Bilateral temporal artery biopsy compatible with temporal arteritis
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Although the results showed no giant cells, there was evidence of active non-granulomatous vasculitis and confirmed bilateral temporal arteritis within the context of the clinical setting

confirmatory_findings.finding: Rapid clinical response to high-dose steroids
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: increased prednisone to 60 mg daily; on day two post-admission ... significantly decreased pain in the temporal region
